10.1002_adfm.202531269: Lithium–sulfur (Li─S) batteries are hindered by lithium polysulfide (LiPS) shuttling and sluggish redox kinetics, demanding catalysts that both anchor LiPS and accelerate their conversion. Here, we introduce anion‐tailored asymmetry engineering of MoS 2 via controlled Se and Te substitution. The intrinsic size mismatch of S/Se/Te induces lattice and electronic asymmetry, weakening in‐plane covalent bonds and creating localized electronic states. In addition, the dual effects lead to more exposure of additional edge sites and activates inert basal planes, enabling concurrent catalytic activity. Consequently, the optimized MoS 1.75 Te 0.25 –S cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1486.2 mAh g −1 (0.1 C) and 537.6 mAh g −1 (1.0 C) after 3000 cycles and 382.9 mAh g −1 after 3000 cycles at 3.0 C, indicating an ultralow decay rate of 0.012% per cycle. Even at a high sulfur loading, it sustains robust capacity retention, underscoring strong practical promise. These results establish anion‐tailored asymmetry engineering as a generalizable strategy, providing mechanistic insights and design principles for advanced Li─S batteries.
10.1002_adma.75487: Developing highly active and stable Ru‐based catalysts for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is essential to accelerate the industrialization of proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE). However, Ru‐based catalysts inevitably follow the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) during the actual reaction, which in turn triggers severe Ru dissolution. While shifting the reaction pathway to the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) improves stability, it often compromises catalytic activity. Herein, we design an Nb‐doped Ru/RuO 2 heterostructure catalyst to inhibit the unstable LOM, and concurrently propose a favorable Brønsted Site‐Promoted Proton Transfer (BSPT) mechanism derived from the AEM. Specifically, the synergy between Nb doping and Ru/RuO 2 heterostructure enhances activity by improving deprotonation capability and optimizing oxygen‐intermediate adsorption, while simultaneously improving durability by stabilizing lattice oxygen and suppressing excessive oxidation and dissolution of Ru. Consequently, the Nb‐Ru/RuO 2 delivers an overpotential of 186 mV at 10 mA cm −2 with impressive durability over 3000 h. In a working PEMWE, it exhibits remarkable durability for 3000, 1200, and 900 h at 500, 1000, and 2000 mA cm −2 . This study offers novel design principles and theoretical foundations to advance efficient, low‐cost PEMWE hydrogen production.
10.1016_j.gee.2026.07.009: Aqueous organic redox flow batteries (AORFBs) are a highly promising electrochemical technology for large-scale energy storage but limited by ion exchange membranes (IEMs) durability. However, the mechanical and chemical structure degradation of IEMs is a key yet largely overlooked limiting lifetime. Here, we propose a methyl-engineering strategy for a sulfonated poly(indole ketone) (SPIK) membrane (designated as M-SPIK x/y), which, by simply tuning the x/y ratio, modulates electrostatic repulsion and π-π stacking among chain segments to induce adaptive self-assembly into an ordered structure. The membrane with this ordered architecture exhibits good mechanical integrity and strong resistance to chemical degradation, suggesting its potential resistance to the “mechanical-chemical” coupling failure that typically plagues long-term cycling. The optimized M-SPIK 60/40 membrane achieved an exceptional mechanical strength of 99.98 MPa and a high K + conductivity of 35.63 mS cm -1 at 30 °C. Regarding stability, the membrane showed no detectable chemical degradation even after 500 h in 0.1 M KOH at 50 °C, confirming its outstanding chemical stability under high-temperature alkaline conditions. When assembled in an AORFB, the battery equipped with the M-SPIK 60/40 membrane delivered over 1200 cycles (580 h), more than doubling the lifetime of its unmodified counterpart. Remarkably, it maintained stable energy efficiency above 80% over 700 cycles even at 50 °C. This work establishes methyl-engineered ordered assembly as a powerful strategy to mitigate the mechanical-chemical coupling failure, enabling the construction of long-lifetime IEMs for grid-scale AORFBs.
10.1021_acscatal.6c05142: 2,5-bishydroxymethylfuran (BHMF) is a key bio-monomer that can be obtained by the electrochemical reduction of 5-(hydroxymethyl)furfural (HMF), bypassing the need for molecular hydrogen. Mildly alkaline conditions favor BHMF over hydrogenolysis products; however, on the cheapest Cu electrodes, they also promote side reactions such as hydrodimerization into 5,5'-bis(hydroxymethyl)hydrofuroin (BHH) and oligomerization at HMF concentrations above 20mM, thus hindering process scalability. The mechanistic understanding of HMF electroreduction under mildly basic conditions remains limited compared to acidic environments, preventing rational improvements in selectivity at industrially relevant concentrations. In this work, using a combination of experimental and computational studies, we investigated the competition between BHMF formation and unwanted hydrodimerization into BHH at pH 9.2 on Cu foam electrocatalysts with different electroactive surface area. Our findings reveal that BHH formation and carbon loss (C-loss) by oligomerization originate from two distinct pathways. The dimerization results from the surface-catalyzed C-C coupling of two HMF adsorbates, whereas oligomerization is related to the desorption of the ketyl intermediate into the double layer, a process increasingly favored at more cathodic potentials. In contrast, BHMF formation proceeds preferably via hydrogenation of an alkoxyl intermediate. The contribution of each pathway is modified with the electroactive Cu surface area. A larger surface area of the Cu foam, obtained by Cu nanoparticles electrodeposition, results in an increase in BHMF selectivity from 40% to 58% at 50mM HMF and a remarkable decrease of the oligomerization when performing the reaction at -0.51V vs RHE. Our findings provide mechanistic insight into how catalyst morphology and electrochemical conditions control selectivity in HMF electroreduction for Cu electrocatalysts, offering design principles to optimize BHMF production while minimizing hydrodimerization and carbon loss by oligomerization.
10.1021_acsnano.6c09648: Nanoplastics are emerging pollutants of global concern, yet their quantitative in vivo fate in terrestrial vertebrates remains poorly resolved owing to analytical limitations. Here, we constructed a quantitative whole-body fate map in laying hens orally exposed to backbone 14C-labeled polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs) at 0.4 mg kg-1 day-1, a dose selected to represent an environmentally plausible upper-bound exposure scenario. The 14C-PS-NPs had an approximately 80 nm dry-state primary particle diameter, while the vacuum-dried dosing material showed micrometer-scale agglomeration upon standardized redispersion. Excreta represented the dominant compartment in the mass balance, accounting for 88.55 ± 0.54% and 90.06 ± 1.02% of the cumulative administered dose after 3- and 7-day exposures, respectively. Gastrointestinal contents constituted the largest residual nonexcreted compartment, whereas kidney, liver, and lung showed the most prominent 14C signals among internal organs. Trace brain-associated 14C was below the matrix-specific LOD at day 3 but quantifiable at day 7, and the overall egg-associated signal remained below 0.1% of the cumulative administered dose. In a complementary 21-day dietary study, laying hens were exposed to PS-NPs at 0.4 and 2 mg kg-1 day-1 to assess intestinal responses together with circulating and selected-organ readouts. The 21-day study showed intestinal histopathological changes, elevated permeability markers, and pro-inflammatory and oxidative-stress readouts, while cecal microbiota compositional shifts were most evident in the 2 mg kg-1 day-1 group. This study provides a quantitative whole-body fate map of PS-derived 14C together with an assessment of biological responses to repeated dietary PS-NP exposure in laying hens.
10.1039_d5ta10024k: Non-equimolar B-site-engineered La(TiMnFeCo)O 3 medium-entropy perovskites outperform equimolar variants, enabling high performance for supercapacitor electrodes and piezoelectric energy harvesting (PENG).
10.1109_tpel.2026.3658337: To adapt to a wider range of application prospects, automatic guided vehicles (AGVs) need to have multiple charging methods. In this paper, a four-port integrated wired/wireless charging system for power and auxiliary batteries in AGVs is proposed. In the wired mode, the DC source can be connected to the compensating capacitor in parallel. In the wireless mode, a receiving coil with a series compensating capacitor is used to receive energy from the primary transmitting coil. In this way, the wired and wireless charging systems are integrated in the secondary side. The power and auxiliary batteries are connected to the H-bridge converter on different ports. Such an integrated design allows both batteries to be charged simultaneously. In addition, the power and auxiliary batteries can be powered in both directions in case of an emergency. Mathematical models of the proposed system are developed, and the working principles are discussed. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed system, experimental prototypes are established. The agreement between experimental and mathematical results indicates the effectiveness of the proposed system.
10.31635_ccschem.026.202507155: Organic anode materials for sodium-ion batteries are attracting a great deal of interest due to their sustainability and design flexibility. However, the Na+ insertion mechanism is poorly understood, especially for disordered organic anode materials. A lack of understanding restricts optimization efforts and potential commercialization. Herein, we apply a range of characterization techniques, such as three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED), powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), Raman spectroscopy, electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy (EPR), and pair distribution function (PDF) analysis to a model system, sodium naphthalene-2,6-dicarboxylate (Na2NDC) to elucidate the Na+ storage mechanism. A combined Ab initio Random Structure Search (AIRSS) and PDF study was conducted to postulate a structure of sodiated Na2+xNDC (s-NDC). Our work reveals an expansion in the Na+-O storage layer, to allow for accommodation of inserted Na+. Meanwhile, the naphthalene units exist as radical species, promoting a re-orientation to accommodate the inserted Na+, and facilitating a stabilizing π interaction. Ultimately, our results illustrate the efficacy of using a multitechnique approach to study the sodiation mechanism of organic electrodes and offer insight into the sodiated structure. This approach can inform the strategic molecular design of future organic anode materials.
